newsitem.title: UK: Inchcape sells Bain Hogg, wipes debt.
newsitem.headline: Inchcape sells Bain Hogg, wipes debt.

text.p: Struggling international trading group Inchcape said Tuesday it had sold its insurance broking arm Bain Hogg to U.S. broking giant Aon Corp., completing a plan designed to clear hundreds of millions of dollars in debts and refocus the group more on its core distribution businesses.

Aon, the second biggest insurance broker in the world, is to pay 160 million pounds ($253 million) for Bain Hogg, which has a significant share of the hard pressed British retail insurance market, where premiums have been falling and growth is elusive.
Inchcape said only three weeks ago it would probably spin off Bain Hogg in order to reduce group borrowings.
But on Tuesday it said it believed the sale price to Aon represented better value than a spin-off. However, some analysts wondered if Bain Hogg was not worth more.

Aon is likely to integrate Bain Hogg with its other British insurance broking interests, wholesale reinsurance specialist Nicholson Jenner Leslie and Aon Risk Services, a much smaller retail broking operation, industry sources said.

This should result in substantial cost savings. Staff numbers in the combined operation would probably be cut. Bain Hogg employs 4,500 people worldwide, while Aon's British activities have a 3,000 strong workforce, the industry sources said.
